bluf: Big Leap is a Utah SEO, content and digital PR agency, founded 2008, selling brand led performance marketing to mid market clients with AI SEO woven into a search first mix. Its house practises what it sells: llms.txt published, 42 Google ads in the Transparency Center, 12 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days. Where it is going is not written down: the record lists no moves, news, jobs or pricing. The one thing a rival should know: all 14 named clients are names only, so the 95.3% retention claim on its homepage is likely the whole pitch.
doing:
The positioning line, in the record's words, is a Utah agency selling brand led performance marketing: SEO with AI SEO woven in, content, digital PR and paid media, with RevOps alignment. In plain words, a search agency that has bolted paid media and a revenue operations line onto its SEO core and leads with retention rather than results. The headline claim is that it reports 95.3% client retention; the record holds no audit of the figure.

SEO leads the sold mix (score 3: SEO leads the homepage title and meta, with technical, local and migration pages and dozens of SEO case studies). Four core lines sit at score 2: AI Search / GEO (an AI SEO page plus B2B, SaaS, ecommerce, local and service business AI SEO pages, and an Awardco digital PR GEO case), Content & Digital PR (content marketing cases such as Visionworks), Local (GBP at scale for multi location and franchise brands, with Avis, Pinnacle Roofing and Urban Orthodontics cases) and Paid Search (a paid search page for mid enterprise brands and a Google Ads agency page). The record lists no proprietary products and no partners.

Its AI posture is AI SEO woven into the mix, with AI search pages for B2B, SaaS, ecommerce, local and service businesses. The house corroborates it (llms.txt, 15 AI topic URLs in the sitemap), but no audited AI visibility product shows (P1 partial) and AI Automation / Agents scores 0.

The record lists no moves, news, deepened case studies or job postings: for an agency founded in 2008 that silence is a finding. No pricing signals show (P5 unknown). Also absent for a company of its kind: Web & Product, Retail Media and Data & Measurement all score 0, so the migration pages it sells rest on no build capability the record can see.
clients:
The record describes a mid market client type, verticals from multi location and franchise, ecommerce and DTC and B2B and SaaS through automotive, contractors, HVAC and roofing, finance and insurance, healthcare and mental health, legal, higher education and manufacturing, and a US home market with Utah the only office listed.

The book holds 14 clients, 12 from case studies and 2 from slugs, and every one is a name only (named only 14 of 14, observed 0). Avis, Extra Space Storage, Workfront, Venafi, Visionworks, The Honest Company, Alphagraphics, Paul Mitchell Schools, Nu Skin, Awardco, Pinnacle Roofing and Abbey Neuropsychology Clinic carry case study URLs; Pluralsight and Purple appear as slugs. With no signal describing the work, each need is inferred from what the agency leads with: organic demand first, local and lead generation for the multi location names (the Local note cites Avis and Pinnacle Roofing), PR, reputation and content for Visionworks and Awardco (the Content & Digital PR note cites both), and AI and automation for Awardco, whose digital PR GEO case the AI Search note names.

Two clients also sit on other tracked agencies' books: The Honest Company on tinuiti and Purple on siege-media, 2 shared of the 14.

What the base needs next, against the edition's judgments: it is likely, with moderate confidence, that the multi location names ask for the local work KJ6 (The agency middle is being hollowed out) prices down and for the P3 move the record shows as partial, and a roughly even chance that the B2B and SaaS names (Workfront, Venafi, Pluralsight, Awardco) ask for audited AI visibility under KJ1 (The click is being replaced by the citation), which Big Leap sells but has not made a product.
house: Say and do: the Radar tested 3 sold lines against Big Leap's own house and all 3 are corroborated. AI Search / GEO: it publishes llms.txt and its sitemap holds 15 AI topic URLs. Paid Search: it runs its own Google ads, 42 in the Transparency Center and 11 in the last 30 days, last shown 2026-09-26, under the advertiser names BIG LEAP, LLC and TIGRANUHI BAGHDASARYAN; a sample reads 'Zero Friction Pro - Learn More About Us | Big Leap's Digital Marketing Agency Faqs'. Publishing cadence: 12 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days and 98 in 365, from 565 URLs. No gaps flagged. Tags are gtm, hubspot and vwo, vwo the only test tool, on WordPress; no social pixels, no Meta or TikTok ad presence recorded. It blocks no AI crawlers. LinkedIn ads: none found, 0 company and 0 thought leader ads.
market:
The Horus read: tailwind index -0.8, band Neutral, 17th percentile, resilience 28.5, say/do integrity 100. Best placed for KJ1 (The click is being replaced by the citation, net 0.257), driven by AI Search / GEO at +2 and Content & Digital PR at +1, and for KJ2 (ads inside AI answers, net 0.206). Most exposed to KJ6 (The agency middle is being hollowed out, net -0.318), SEO, Paid Search and Content & Digital PR each at -1, and to KJ4 (The platforms are absorbing the execution layer, net -0.206). Best fit: The Toll Road at 41/100. P moves: partial on P1, P3, P4 and P7; absent on P2, P6 and P8; unknown on P5.

The Monsoon read: index 58.6, band Onshore wind, 64th percentile, migration 56.1 against displacement 61.1. The verdict puts 56 of the index on the sold mix, SEO (16) and Local (10) carrying the most movable hours, and sends 65% of the work to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America. The class is inferred: no hub offices, no onshore claims.
openings:
The strongest opening is the audited AI visibility product it lacks. Big Leap sells AI SEO across B2B, SaaS, ecommerce, local and service business pages, yet no tracking, scorecard or citation share product shows (P1 partial). It is likely, with moderate confidence, that a rival leading with a measured citation share number takes the AI conversation in the B2B and SaaS accounts (Workfront, Venafi, Pluralsight, Awardco). The falsifier: a Big Leap page publishing an AI citation or visibility metric with a method.

Price next. No public pricing model shows (P5 unknown) and the Monsoon displacement read is 61.1: a transparent, outcome priced offer is very likely to force a conversation Big Leap cannot have in public, and an offshore delivered rival can likely undercut the SEO and Local hours, though that read is inferred.

Then the book. All 14 clients are names only; The Honest Company (also on tinuiti) and Purple (also on siege-media) already shop. Multi location is contestable on P3 (no LSA or Sponsored Places work), paid media on P4 and P8 (no first party data, creative volume or measurement depth, no ads inside assistants), and the feeds and entity layer (P2 absent) is unclaimed.
watch: I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, next reading October 2026: output or outcome pricing announced at a top five holdco would deepen the KJ6 exposure on Big Leap's SEO and paid search hours.

I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, late October 2026: search and other growth below 10% flags cannibalization of the SEO core, while growth above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and favours its KJ1 and KJ2 tailwinds.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk behind KJ1.
I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the next milestone ($2B) and any pricing below $20 CPM would change the KJ2 read on its paid search line.
No dated move sits in the record to follow up, so the item to watch is whether any move, job posting or pricing page appears at all before the next compile.
The next Radar compile refreshes offices, ads, sitemap cadence and clients, and this dossier is only as fresh as the 2026-09-28 compile.
